questions.title: What is batch processing in OData V2, and what benefits does it bring?
questions.description: Normally each OData operation is sent in its own HTTP request. Batch processing is an optional feature that lets a client group several operations into a single HTTP request: a POST to the service's $batch endpoint whose body is a multipart MIME message, one part per operation. The benefits are fewer round trips, because many reads and changes travel in one request and one response, and atomic changes: insert, update and delete operations can be grouped into a ChangeSet, which the server applies all together or not at all. The server processes the parts in the order they appear, and answers with one multipart response containing a response for each part, in the same order.
keyPoints: Several operations in one HTTP request: POST <service root>/$batch.
Body is a multipart/mixed MIME message, one part per operation.
Benefit: fewer round trips.
Benefit: ChangeSets make a group of changes atomic (all or nothing).
Responses come back in one multipart response, in request order.

questions.title: Which HTTP headers does an OData V2 batch request need?
questions.description: A batch request is a single HTTP POST to the $batch endpoint of the service. It must carry a Content-Type header with the value multipart/mixed and a boundary specification; the boundary string (often a GUID such as batch_36522ad7-...) separates the parts of the body, and it must be quoted if it contains special characters such as ( ) < > @ , ; : / " [ ] ? =. The request may also contain DataServiceVersion and MaxDataServiceVersion headers, or other HTTP headers that apply to the whole batch. Inside the body, each part for a retrieve request or a ChangeSet carries its own MIME headers: Content-Type (application/http for a single request, multipart/mixed with its own boundary for a ChangeSet) and Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary.
keyPoints: POST <service root>/$batch.
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=<boundary>.
Quote the boundary if it contains special characters.
Optional DataServiceVersion / MaxDataServiceVersion for the whole batch.
Each part: Content-Type (application/http or multipart/mixed) and Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary.

examples.title: Batch request headers
examples.code:
POST /OData/OData.svc/$batch HTTP/1.1
Host: services.odata.org
DataServiceVersion: 1.0
MaxDataServiceVersion: 2.0
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b

<Batch Request Body>

questions.title: How is a batch request body structured, what is a ChangeSet, and how does Content-ID referencing work?
questions.description: The body of a batch request is an ordered series of retrieve operations and ChangeSets, each in its own MIME part separated by the batch boundary. A ChangeSet is an atomic unit of work made of an unordered group of one or more insert, update or delete operations; it cannot contain retrieve requests and cannot be nested. A ChangeSet part is itself a multipart MIME document with its own changeset boundary and one part per operation. The order of ChangeSets and retrieve requests in the batch is significant, while the order of requests inside a ChangeSet is not, and the server must apply all requests of a ChangeSet or none of them. If an insert request inside a ChangeSet carries a Content-ID header, later requests in the same ChangeSet can refer to the new entity as $ followed by that value, for example POST $1/Orders, which creates an order for the customer inserted under Content-ID 1.
keyPoints: Body = ordered retrieve requests and ChangeSets, separated by the batch boundary.
ChangeSet = atomic group of inserts/updates/deletes; no GETs, no nesting.
A ChangeSet is a nested multipart part with its own boundary.
Batch order matters; order inside a ChangeSet does not.
Content-ID: n on an insert, then $n in later requests of the same ChangeSet.

examples.title: Batch with a retrieve request and a ChangeSet using Content-ID
examples.code:
POST /service/$batch HTTP/1.1
Host: host
DataServiceVersion: 1.0
MaxDataServiceVersion: 2.0
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b

--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

GET /service/Customers('ALFKI') HTTP/1.1
Host: host

--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621

--changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
Content-ID: 1

POST /service/Customers HTTP/1.1
Host: host
Content-Type: application/atom+xml;type=entry

<new Customer>
--changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

POST $1/Orders HTTP/1.1
Host: host
Content-Type: application/atom+xml;type=entry

<new Order for the Customer created above>
--changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621--
--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b--

questions.title: What does a batch response look like (headers and body)?
questions.description: If the headers of a batch request are valid, the server returns 202 Accepted, which means the request was accepted for processing; individual requests inside it may still fail. A batch with invalid headers gets a 4xx response and is not processed. The batch response must have a Content-Type header of multipart/mixed with a boundary, which may differ from the request's boundary. The body mirrors the request: it contains one response per retrieve request and per ChangeSet, in the same order as in the request. Each part has Content-Type: application/http and Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary, and holds an HTTP response formatted exactly as it would be outside a batch. For a ChangeSet the body contains either the responses for all its successfully processed requests, or a single response indicating that the whole ChangeSet failed.
keyPoints: Status 202 Accepted when the batch headers are valid; 4xx if they are invalid.
Content-Type: multipart/mixed with a (possibly different) boundary.
One response per retrieve request and per ChangeSet, in request order.
Each part: application/http, binary, containing a normal HTTP response.
ChangeSet: all individual responses, or one failure response for the whole set.

examples.title: Batch response: one read OK, ChangeSet OK, last read 404
examples.code:
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
DataServiceVersion: 1.0
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b

--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

HTTP/1.1 200 Ok
Content-Type: application/atom+xml;type=entry

<Customer ALFKI>
--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621

--changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: http://host/service.svc/Customer('POIUY')

<new Customer>
--changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
--changeset_77162fcd-b8da-41ac-a9f8-9357efbbd621--
--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/xml

<Error message>
--batch_36522ad7-fc75-4b56-8c71-56071383e77b--
